title: Creating IAM Roles for AWS: Tree Discovery, Asset Discovery, and Scanning

blocks.text: To enable Tree Discovery, asset discovery, and scanning for your AWS accounts, you must create dedicated IAM roles that grant the necessary read-only and discovery permissions. This section explains how to set up these roles from the AWS Portal, defining the trust policy, attaching the required inline policy, and assigning a consistent role name, so each role is correctly recognized during configuration.
If you are onboarding multiple AWS accounts, repeat the full procedure manually for each one.
Ensure you have the following information before you start creating roles:

blocks.item: Have access to the AWS Portal with permissions to create IAM roles and policies.
Keep the trust policy and inline policy JSON ready to copy and paste (provided separately per role type).
Know which target accounts you are configuring. If you are configuring multiple accounts, this entire procedure must be repeated manually in each one.

blocks.text: To create IAM Role in AWS IAM Console, do the following:

blocks.item: 1. Create the IAM Role with a Custom Trust Policy.
To create IAM roles in the AWS IAM console, do the following:
Sign in to the AWS IAM Console.
In the left navigation pane, go to IAM > Roles > Create role.
Under Select trusted entity, choose Custom trust policy.
Paste the Trust Policy JSON text copied from your AI Security Console into the Policy Editor and click Next.
See image.
2. Attach the Policy.
To attach the policy, do the following:
1. On the Add permissions page, look under Permissions policies.
2. Use the Filter by Type drop-down menu and select the required policy type, e.g., AWS managed - job function.
3. Search for and select the checkbox next to the Policy Name, e.g., ReadOnlyAccess, and then click Next.
3. Create the Role.
To create a role, do the following:
On the Name, review, and create page, do the following:
Role Name: Enter the exact role name required by your AI Security Console.
Ensure there are no trailing spaces or typos, as this name must match your discovery configuration later.
Description: Add a brief description for the role.
Click Create role.
4. Add the Inline Permissions Policy.
To add the inline permissions policy, do the following:
Click View role in the confirmation banner (or search for the role name in Roles and click it).
Copy the Inline Permissions Policy JSON from your AI Security Console.
Under the Permissions policies tab, click the Add permissions drop-down menu on the right and select Create inline policy.
See image.
In the Policy editor, switch to the JSON tab.
Paste the copied inline policy JSON (replacing any default placeholder text) and click Next.
See image.
On the Review and create page, enter a descriptive Policy name (e.g., AISecurityDiscoveryInlinePolicy) and click Create policy.
See image.
